output.summary: KEP-2290 proposed a new `ok-to-test` label, applied to non-member PRs after a trusted reviewer comments `/ok-to-test`, so the trigger plugin can determine PR trust from a label instead of scanning every comment. The KEP is marked implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Identifying untrusted PRs was easy via the `needs-ok-to-test` label, but finding a `/ok-to-test` comment meant scanning every comment, adding code complexity and API token use. The proposal adds an `ok-to-test` label that is required on non-member PRs before the trigger plugin starts tests, and applies it through a single GenericCommentEvent handler. The KEP does not change the process for organization members.

alternatives.option: Keep scanning all PR comments for `/ok-to-test` to determine trust
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this 'is difficult and involves scanning every comment for a `/ok-to-test`, which increases code complexity and API token consumption.'

evidence.quote: However the contrary is difficult and involves scanning every comment for a `/ok-to-test`, which increases code complexity and API token consumption.
We suggest introducing a new label named `ok-to-test` that would be required on any non-member PR before automatic test jobs can be started by the `trigger` plugin.
This KEP will not change the current process for members of the organization.
